name: Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1948–1997) from Faisalabad, Punjab. Widely regarded as the greatest qawwali singer in history, he brought Sufi devotional music to global audiences through collaborations with Peter Gabriel, Eddie Vedder, and film soundtracks. He received the UNESCO Music Prize in 1995.

name: Abida Parveen
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer (b. 1954) from Larkana, Sindh. Trained by her father Ustad Ghulam Haider, she is the foremost interpreter of Sindhi, Punjabi, Saraiki, and Urdu Sufi poetry. She has been called the 'Queen of Sufi Music' and received the Hilal-i-Imtiaz, Pakistan's second-highest civilian honor.

name: Ghulam Farid Sabri
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1930–1994), elder of the Sabri Brothers. Along with his brother Maqbool Ahmed, he popularized qawwali through studio recordings and international tours beginning in the 1950s. Their rendition of 'Tajdar-e-Haram' remains one of the most recognized qawwali recordings worldwide.

name: Maqbool Ahmed Sabri
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1945–2011), younger of the Sabri Brothers. Together with Ghulam Farid Sabri, he formed one of the most commercially successful and internationally touring qawwali groups in history, recording extensively for EMI Pakistan and performing at venues worldwide.

name: Aziz Mian Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1942–2000) from Delhi (migrated to Pakistan post-partition). Known for his intense, improvisational style and marathon performances, his rendition of 'Hashr Ke Roz Yeh Poochhunga' established him as one of the most powerful voices in qawwali history. He performed extensively in Urdu and Punjabi.

name: Rahat Fateh Ali Khan
biography: Pakistani singer (b. 1974) from Faisalabad, nephew and protégé of Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. He has become one of the most prolific vocalists in South Asian music, performing both classical qawwali and Bollywood playback. He continues the family qawwali lineage spanning over six centuries.

name: Pathanay Khan
biography: Pakistani classical and Sufi singer (1928–2000) from Rajasthan, later settled in Punjab, Pakistan. A master of kafi singing, he was considered the definitive interpreter of Bulleh Shah and Khawaja Ghulam Farid's poetry. His austere, devotional style earned him reverence among purists of Punjabi and Saraiki Sufi music.

name: Faiz Ali Faiz
biography: Pakistani qawwal (b. 1962) from Hyderabad, Sindh. A hereditary qawwal performing at shrines across Pakistan, he gained international recognition through recordings on the Real World label and tours in Europe and North America. His performances emphasize traditional dargah qawwali.

name: Amjad Sabri
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1976–2016) from Karachi, son of Ghulam Farid Sabri. He carried forward the Sabri Brothers' legacy as a solo performer and became one of Pakistan's most beloved devotional singers. He was assassinated in Karachi in 2016.

name: Fareed Ayaz
biography: Pakistani qawwal (b. 1951) who leads the Fareed Ayaz & Abu Muhammad Qawwal ensemble. A descendant of Mian Tansen's musical lineage, he performs qawwali rooted in the Delhi gharana tradition, specializing in Persian, Urdu, and Braj Bhasha compositions. He has performed at festivals worldwide including WOMAD and Fes Festival.

name: Abu Muhammad
biography: Pakistani qawwal (b. 1953) who performs alongside Fareed Ayaz in one of Pakistan's most respected traditional qawwali ensembles. Together they represent the Qawwal Bachchon ka Gharana of Delhi, maintaining centuries-old performance traditions.

name: Puran Chand Wadali
biography: Indian Sufi singer (1937–2023) from Guru Ki Wadali, Amritsar. The elder of the Wadali Brothers duo, he and his brother Pyarelal brought Punjabi Sufi kafis and Sufi-folk music to mainstream audiences in India through concert performances, recordings, and Bollywood soundtracks.

name: Pyarelal Wadali
biography: Indian Sufi singer (1943–2018) from Guru Ki Wadali, Amritsar. The younger of the Wadali Brothers, he was known for his powerful high-register voice. The duo's renditions of Bulleh Shah's kafis and Waris Shah's Heer are considered definitive interpretations.

name: Reshma
biography: Pakistani folk and Sufi singer (1947–2013) originally from a nomadic Rajasthani community in the Thar Desert. Discovered singing at a shrine festival as a teenager, she became one of the most iconic voices of South Asian folk-Sufi music with songs like 'Laal Meri Pat' and 'Lambi Judaai.'

name: Allan Faqir
biography: Pakistani Sindhi Sufi singer (1932–2000) from Jamshoro, Sindh. The foremost interpreter of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai's poetry in the 20th century, he performed at Bhittai's shrine and carried the living tradition of Sindhi Sufi music to wider audiences through radio, television, and concert performances.

name: Sain Zahoor
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer (b. 1937) from Okara, Punjab. A practicing fakir in the Qalandariyya tradition, he gained international recognition after winning the BBC World Music Award in 2006. His ecstatic performance style draws directly from the dhamaal tradition at Sufi shrines.

name: Sanam Marvi
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer (b. 1986) from Hyderabad, Sindh. She rose to prominence through Coke Studio Pakistan and is recognized as a leading contemporary voice for Sindhi and Saraiki Sufi poetry, particularly the works of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai and Sachal Sarmast.

name: Tina Sani
biography: Pakistani ghazal and Sufi singer (b. 1954) from Hyderabad, Sindh. Classically trained, she is renowned for her interpretations of Faiz Ahmed Faiz's poetry and traditional Sufi compositions. She has performed internationally and received the Sitara-i-Imtiaz from the Government of Pakistan.

name: Mehdi Hassan
biography: Pakistani ghazal singer (1927–2012) from Rajasthan, India, who migrated to Pakistan. Known as the 'King of Ghazal,' his mastery of classical raag-based ghazal singing set the gold standard for Urdu vocal music. His renditions of Sufi-influenced ghazals by Rumi, Ghalib, and others are considered definitive.

name: Ghulam Ali
biography: Pakistani ghazal singer (b. 1940) from Hyderabad, Sindh. A master of the Patiala gharana tradition, his recordings of Urdu and Punjabi ghazals and Sufi compositions have made him one of the most popular vocalists in the subcontinent. His voice combines classical precision with emotional depth.

name: Munshi Raziuddin Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1927–2006) from Delhi, later based in Karachi. He was one of the most respected traditional qawwals of the 20th century, performing at major dargahs. His ensemble maintained the classical Delhi qawwali repertoire with strict adherence to traditional forms.

name: Bahauddin Khan Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal (1925–2002) from Hyderabad, Sindh. A traditional dargah performer, he was considered one of the finest shrine qawwals of the later 20th century, maintaining repertoire and performance practices closely tied to the Chishti devotional tradition.

name: Meraj Ahmed Nizami
biography: Indian qawwal based at the dargah of Nizamuddin Auliya in Delhi. A hereditary Nizami qawwal, he represents the lineage of performers who have sung at this major Chishti shrine for generations, maintaining the traditional qawwali repertoire associated with Amir Khusrau.

name: Tahira Syed
biography: Pakistani classical and Sufi singer (b. 1956) from Lahore. Daughter of singer Malika Pukhraj, she is trained in Hindustani classical music and is known for her refined interpretations of Sufi poetry, particularly ghazals and kafis in Urdu and Punjabi.

name: Rizwan-Muazzam Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwali duo consisting of Rizwan Ali Khan and Muazzam Ali Khan, nephews of Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan from Faisalabad. They carry forward the family's qawwali lineage and have recorded extensively, performing at international festivals while maintaining the traditional repertoire.

name: Attaullah Khan Esakhelvi
biography: Pakistani folk and Sufi singer (b. 1951) from Isakhel, Punjab. One of the most prolific recording artists in Pakistani music history with thousands of songs, his repertoire spans Punjabi, Saraiki, and Urdu folk-Sufi traditions. His emotionally charged vocal style draws from the Sufi dhamaal tradition.

name: Sher Miandad Khan
biography: Pakistani qawwal (b. 1955) from a hereditary qawwal family. He is known for powerful renditions of traditional qawwali and devotional music performed at major shrines across Pakistan, including the dargahs at Pakpattan and Data Darbar in Lahore.

name: Nayyara Noor
biography: Pakistani playback and ghazal singer (1950–2022) from Assam, India. Known as 'Bulbul-e-Pakistan' (Nightingale of Pakistan), she was celebrated for her interpretations of Sufi-influenced poetry by Faiz Ahmed Faiz, Ghalib, and others. Her pure vocal tone and emotional sincerity defined an era of Pakistani music.

name: Akhtar Sharif Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal known for his performances at major Sufi shrines in Punjab and Sindh. He represents the traditional dargah qawwali tradition, performing devotional compositions in Urdu, Punjabi, and Persian at urs celebrations and weekly mehfils.

name: Mehr Ali & Sher Ali
biography: Pakistani qawwali duo from a hereditary qawwal family. They are recognized for traditional devotional performances at shrines and recording studios, performing the classical qawwali repertoire in Urdu, Punjabi, and Persian with a style rooted in the devotional shrine tradition.

name: Nooran Sisters
biography: Indian Sufi singing duo consisting of Jyoti Nooran (b. 1996) and Sultana Nooran (b. 1994) from Jalandhar, Punjab. They gained widespread recognition through their performances of Punjabi Sufi music, including appearances on Coke Studio and Bollywood films.

name: Mubarak Ali Khan
biography: Pakistani classical singer (1925–2001) from the Sham Chaurasi gharana in Punjab. A master of khayal and Sufi kafi singing, he was one of the foremost interpreters of traditional Punjabi Sufi poetry in a classical vocal framework. He was the father of singer Hamid Ali Khan.

name: Asif Ali Santoo Khan
biography: Pakistani qawwal and Sufi singer from a musical family in Punjab. He is known for powerful and energetic performances of Punjabi Sufi music and qawwali, particularly at shrine festivals, and has released recordings blending traditional devotional music with contemporary production.

name: Arif Feroz Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal from Lahore known for devotional performances at Data Darbar and other major shrines. His repertoire includes traditional manqabat, hamd, and naat compositions in the classical qawwali style.

name: Mukhtiar Ali
biography: Indian Sufi folk singer from Bikaner, Rajasthan. He performs Sufi poetry of Kabir, Bulleh Shah, and Shah Abdul Latif in a raw, unaccompanied vocal style rooted in the Manganiyar folk tradition. He has performed at international festivals and is recognized for preserving desert Sufi musical traditions.

name: Mame Khan
biography: Indian Sufi folk singer (b. 1976) from a Manganiyar musical family in Rajasthan. He has brought Rajasthani Sufi and devotional music to global stages including SXSW, Glastonbury, and major international festivals. He performs in Rajasthani, Hindi, and Sindhi.

name: Jafar Hussain Badayuni
biography: Indian qawwal from Badayun, Uttar Pradesh. Descended from a hereditary qawwal family, he performs at the dargah of Nizamuddin Auliya in Delhi and represents the traditional North Indian qawwali lineage with a repertoire in Persian, Urdu, and Hindi.

name: Iqbal Bahu
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer known for his renditions of Sultan Bahoo's abyat and other Punjabi Sufi poetry. He performs in the traditional style associated with Punjabi Sufi shrines and is recognized for his devotional interpretations of Bahoo's mystical verse.

name: Ali Haider
biography: Pakistani pop and Sufi singer (b. 1974) from Lahore. Initially known as a pop vocalist, he transitioned to devotional and Sufi music, releasing naats and Sufi compositions. His crossover brought Sufi-influenced music to younger Pakistani audiences.

name: Shafqat Amanat Ali
biography: Pakistani singer (b. 1965) from Lahore, son of Ustad Amanat Ali Khan. Trained in classical music, he performs ghazals and Sufi compositions with classical rigor. His renditions of Sufi poetry on Coke Studio and in Bollywood films have reached large audiences.

name: Raees Khan Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal from the traditional qawwali performance circuit. Known for his energetic shrine performances, he carries the tradition of devotional qawwali at urs celebrations and weekly gatherings at major dargahs in Pakistan.

name: Hamza Akram Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal (b. 1989) from Lahore, a young practitioner of traditional qawwali. He has performed at international venues including the Royal Albert Hall and represents the next generation of qawwali performers maintaining the classical repertoire while reaching global audiences.

name: Malika Pukhraj
biography: Pakistani singer (1912–2004) from Jammu. One of the most celebrated female vocalists in South Asian music history, she performed ghazals, folk songs, and Sufi compositions. Her autobiography 'Song Sung True' documents her remarkable life spanning the British Raj, Partition, and modern Pakistan.

name: Sain Akhtar
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer from Sindh, known for devotional performances at Sufi shrines. He performs in the traditional style of Sindhi shrine music, interpreting the poetry of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai and other Sindhi Sufi masters.

name: Zeb Bangash
biography: Pakistani singer (b. 1982) of Pashtun heritage, known for her performances of Sufi and folk compositions in Pashto, Dari, Urdu, and Punjabi. A graduate of Berklee College of Music, she blends traditional South and Central Asian musical forms with contemporary sensibilities.

name: Abida Hussain
biography: Pakistani Sufi singer from Punjab, recognized for her interpretations of Punjabi and Saraiki Sufi poetry. She performs in the kafi tradition, bringing the works of Bulleh Shah and Sultan Bahoo to devotional audiences.

name: Haji Ghulam Farid Sabri
biography: Pakistani qawwal (early 20th century), patriarch of the Sabri Brothers' musical lineage and father of Ghulam Farid and Maqbool Ahmed Sabri. He established the family qawwali tradition in Karachi and trained his sons in the classical qawwali repertoire.

name: Ustad Bahauddin Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal recognized for traditional devotional performances at shrines across Pakistan. Part of the hereditary qawwal tradition, his ensemble maintains the classical Persian and Urdu qawwali repertoire associated with the Chishti devotional practice.

name: Munir Hussain Qawwal
biography: Pakistani qawwal from Punjab known for his powerful and passionate devotional performances. He is part of the broader qawwali performance tradition in Pakistan, performing at shrine festivals and devotional gatherings.

name: Hans Raj Hans
biography: Indian Sufi and folk singer (b. 1962) from Jalandhar, Punjab. A disciple of Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, he performs Punjabi Sufi kafis and folk songs. He has recorded extensively and brought Punjabi Sufi music to Bollywood and mainstream Indian audiences.
